OPIOID TREATMENT PROGRAM — INITIAL INTAKE ASSESSMENT

Certified OTP: Riverside Comprehensive Treatment Center (SAMHSA/DEA certified opioid treatment program)
Evaluating clinician: Dr. A. Ferrante, MD, Addiction Medicine, with L. Nguyen, LCSW (counselor)

Patient: 34-year-old male, presents voluntarily for evaluation of opioid use disorder and interest in methadone maintenance treatment.

HPI: Patient reports 8 years of escalating heroin and non-prescribed fentanyl use, currently using intravenously 3-4 times daily, with strong cravings, inability to cut down despite multiple attempts, tolerance, and withdrawal symptoms (myalgia, rhinorrhea, GI upset, anxiety) when he tries to stop. Meets DSM-5 criteria for severe Opioid Use Disorder (11/11 criteria endorsed: tolerance, withdrawal, use in larger amounts than intended, unsuccessful efforts to cut down, significant time spent obtaining/using, craving, failure to fulfill role obligations, continued use despite social problems, activities given up, use in hazardous situations, continued use despite physical/psychological problems). He is currently physiologically dependent on opioids as confirmed on exam (see below) and urine toxicology positive for fentanyl and 6-MAM.

Patient states he wants to enroll voluntarily in methadone maintenance treatment; he was informed of alternative options including buprenorphine and naltrexone and states he prefers methadone given prior partial response to buprenorphine.

Medical history: Hepatitis C diagnosed 2019, not yet treated; asthma, no current pregnancy (patient is male); no history of TB; remote history of endocarditis in 2021 treated with IV antibiotics, no current cardiac symptoms. No known trauma history beyond childhood neglect disclosed today. Denies current suicidal ideation.

Psychiatric screening: PHQ-9 score 12 (moderate depression), GAD-7 score 9 (mild anxiety); no active psychosis, no SI/HI. Referral placed for co-located psychiatric consultation.

Physical exam: Vitals stable, BP 128/82, HR 88, afebrile. Track marks bilateral antecubital fossae, healing. Pupils reactive, mild rhinorrhea, mild tremor, diaphoresis, piloerection noted — COWS score 14 (mild-moderate withdrawal). No acute distress. Lungs clear, heart RRR, abdomen benign.

Laboratory: CBC and LFTs drawn today (pending); TB skin test administered today; Hepatitis B/C and HIV serologies sent (HCV Ab positive per prior records, confirmatory RNA pending; HIV negative on point-of-care today). Results will be reviewed at follow-up.

Informed consent: Discussed methadone pharmacology, risks (QTc prolongation, sedation, overdose, drug interactions), benefits (reduction in illicit use, overdose risk, mortality), alternatives (buprenorphine, naltrexone, non-pharmacologic treatment), and expected course of treatment including dosing induction and monitoring. Patient verbalized understanding and signed informed consent form, witnessed and countersigned by clinician.

Treatment plan: Initiation of methadone induction per program protocol starting 30mg, titrating per withdrawal symptoms and vitals. Psychosocial component discussed — patient agreed to weekly individual counseling and expressed interest in a peer support group; referral to onsite counselor completed today.

Withdrawal assessment: COWS 14 today; plan is to begin methadone induction with daily dosing and monitoring for withdrawal/sedation, titrate over first 1-2 weeks under nursing observation.

Safety/overdose assessment: Reviewed overdose risk given recent fentanyl exposure and reduced tolerance risk during induction. Naloxone overdose education provided; patient accepted take-home naloxone kit (Narcan nasal spray x2 doses) dispensed today with instruction on use.

Drug testing: Baseline urine drug screen obtained today per program protocol (positive for fentanyl analogs, opiates); ongoing random drug testing to be performed per OTP schedule in accordance with federal OTP regulations.

Plan: Begin methadone maintenance induction today under nursing supervision; follow up in 48-72 hours for dose adjustment; counseling to begin this week; labs to be reviewed at next visit; continue periodic assessments per program protocol.

All above elements of intake assessment documented in chart and available for review upon request.
